messages:
sam: Quick follow-up from the soak test — saw a scenario where tenant A's compact pass kicked off and we ended up blocking tenant B's microbatches for ~120ms. Full thread with logs below, want to propose a small API split to avoid that.

maria: ugh, can you paste the logs? was that the compaction-run on the host or on the tenant pool?

sam: host-level compaction (compact_slab_worker) triggered while eviction scans were running. excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-19T14:02:11Z] tenant=A compact: candidates=342 free_after=1.2MB
[2026-03-19T14:02:11Z] evictor: scan start tenant=B inflight=12
[2026-03-19T14:02:11Z] compact: acquiring-global-compact-lock
[2026-03-19T14:02:11Z] tenant=B microbatch: stalled wait_for_slab=120ms
```

alex: Interesting. So compact holds a global lock that serializes allocation paths? we assumed compaction would be nonblocking for small microbatches.

jin: Right now compact takes per-arena locks then grabs the global compact mutex for skyline bookkeeping. That global mutex touches allocator freelist pointers and metrics. If compact is long it can delay small alloc/free ops.

natalie: Two thoughts: 1) split the metric updates out of the hot path so compact doesn't hold the global; 2) add a soft-preempt flag so microbatches can steal a small reserve without waiting for compaction.

sam: Proposed API patch sketch: allocator.reserve_soft(tenant_id, size) -> bool. Soft reservations allow microbatches to allocate from an emergency staging pool that bypasses compaction mutex. If false, caller falls back to host staging + queue.

maria: That seems reasonable, but we need to ensure fairness: tenant A shouldn't starve others by constantly using soft reserves to avoid compaction work. How do we enforce quotas?

alex: We can expose quota tokens per-epoch. e.g., soft_quota_per_minute for tenant. allocator returns false when token exhausted. Simple token-bucket.

jin: Another angle: change compaction to be cooperative. Instead of one long compact job we slice it into N small slices and yield between them. That reduces max hold time on the global lock.

sam: I tested cooperative slicing locally. With slice=25ms the stall went from 120ms to ~30ms but throughput for background compaction dropped ~20%. Might be acceptable if we tune thresholds.

natalie: We should combine both: cooperative compaction + soft reserve fallback. Soft-reserve used rarely for tail-latency spikes; compaction slicing reduces average hold time.

maria: Implementation checklist?

sam: Draft plan: 
- allocator: add reserve_soft API (opt-in per-tenant)
- runtime: token-bucket controller + telemetry (soft_reserve_used, soft_deny)
- compactor: implement cooperative yield points + remove metric aggregation from global lock
- observability: surface stall_impact per-tenant and compaction_hold_time histogram

alex: Small code example for reserve_soft config (proto):
```yaml
tenant_policies:
  tenantA:
    soft_reserve_enabled: true
    soft_quota_per_minute: 50  # microbatches
```

jin: Questions on contracts: who owns the fallback path? If reserve_soft fails, runtime should attempt host-staging + immediate fallback to a cheaper model variant, right?

sam: Yes. Fallback policy: reserve_soft -> if false: try host_staging_alloc(size) -> if still failing, route to compatible smaller model (configurable per-route). We need to ensure we don't double-count tokens across these paths.

natalie: Telemetry will be key. We need a new metric soft_reserve_steals and soft_reserve_denied with tenant tag. Also compaction_hold_ms_by_arena.

infra-bot: deploy: CI passed for branch "split-soft-reserve-api". integration tests 12/12.

maria: Nice. Timeline? This should be low risk but we need perf benches and e2e soak.

sam: Plan to land allocator API in two diffs: 1) API stub + token-bucket runtime (no-op compaction changes) -> soak 1 week; 2) compactor cooperativization + telemetry -> soak 2 weeks.

alex: For the API we should add a tiny danger sweater: if tenant abuses soft reserves ( > 95th percentile of allowed steals ) automatically disable for that tenant for 10m and alert onpager.

natalie: Agreed. Ops wants a guardrail. Also add a dry-run mode where soft reservations are counted but not enforced so we can gauge expected usage.

sam: i'll draft the RFC follow-up with these points and a short perf writeup. ppl to review: @maria @alex @jin @natalie.

maria: LGTM. Add a note about backwards compatibility for Dedicated vs Hosted (we should default soft_reserve_enabled=false for Hosted free-tier).

jin: quick question — does this affect K/V cache semantics? if allocations come from emergency pool the KV cache mapping might change locality. We should check kvcache pin behavior.

sam: good catch. I'll add kvcache invariants to the checklist: emergency pool allocations must maintain same pin semantics; if not possible we mark soft_reserve as 'no_kvcache' and route microbatches without KV hits to that path.

natalie: ok cool. thanks.

sam: Action items: sam->RFC diff, alex->quota auto-disable sketch, jin->compactor slice POC, maria->soak plan + dashboards, natalie->ops guardrails. I'll start the diff today.

alex: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: reminder: weekly offload-telemetry meeting tomorrow 10:30am

sam: thanks everyone.
